speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Sit, Master Sturley. Sit, Dick. He has been since six in Bartholomew's stubble, and the dust is still in the cuff.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: I came to the house, since you did not come to the shop.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I had not promised the shop. I did not shut the door.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: The matter is barley. Twenty plots at the north end, and the corn coming in thin.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: The preachers say the fire is a judgment on malting. Malt is the town's living. Let them preach on what we should eat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have walked a hundred miles of short corn. In a thin year they buy it standing, and the poor who would eat barley bread find it gone into the steep. The maltsters should be made to sell.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: Which price have you paid, Master William, for what measure, and in what place?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: None. I have paid none.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: Then you have a sentence, and no bargain under it. Let us hear a buyer before we make an order for the sellers.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Barley bread is what the poor eat, when the barley is still barley. This year it goes to the steep before it is cut. That is the town. It is not a help to your sentence.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: The small kilns in this street malt a few quarters for the drovers. Force every loft open at a price you have not paid, and the small kilns break, and the great cellars are what is left.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: Mistress Anne has the town in two sentences. You had the sermon.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Two-and-twenty shillings the quarter, and it will be thirty by Christmas. What would you have us do, sell at a loss and be burned out besides?

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Hear him. Sell at a loss and be burned out besides. I was in the wool before this man could count, and I know a true sentence at my own table.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I said they should be made to sell. I did not say I had bought.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: And you have not bought. His price is the town's price. It is not a price out of your belt. I will not say it for you a second time.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: Twenty-two. He said twenty-two. You have not said a number of your own.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: Then the answer is none. We may leave the price and come to the paper.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Two gentlemen of the county are to view the losses. They will certify them, so both fires may go into one brief for the Queen's collection.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: One paper. Their names are not for this table.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will give what I can give.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: A man with a great lord's ear might do more than give.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: My lord's ear is kept for plays.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: He has said it. I will not say it for him, and I will not mend it.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Plays. The town asks a brief, and my son keeps a lord for a stage. I have not enjoyed another man's certainty so well in a long year.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: A yes without a sum is a noise. Bring the sum when you have looked, and not before.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I have no certainty. I have a no on the ear, and a yes on what I can spare. I have not looked at the sum.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Then we take the giving, and the ear stays yours. The row will keep till market.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: What you can give is not a sum you have not looked at. Remember that you said can.

speaker: richard_shakespeare
text: He has looked at nothing tonight but the loaf.

speaker: john_shakespeare
text: Eat, and let the gentlemen stay unnamed.

speaker: abraham_sturley
text: Unnamed, and unsummed. Malt is still the town's living when the pulpit has gone home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: None is the price. Can is the giving. The ear is where I said it was.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Then the night is the night. He has paid none. He has not promised the shop. He has promised what he can give.

speaker: richard_quiney
text: Market will do for the row. Tonight was the hearing.
